title: Fix - static class attributes are not rendered underlined
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

This PR fixes the incorrect rendering of static class attributes in a class diagram.

Resolves #5009 

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

It just fixes the regular expression which was wrong. Now it detects the right characters ('$' and '*').

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
- [ ] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/packages/mermaid/src/docs/community/development.md#3-update-documentation) is used for all new features.
- [x] :bookmark: targeted `develop` branch

Please let me know if i missed something!
author: SteffenLm

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: I'm not familiar with the specifics of class diagram syntax. Based on the docs, this change looks good. But, doesn't this change break diagrams that had `?` previously? @knsv thoughts?

comments.author: SteffenLm
comments.body: Thanks! Idk if the `?` was done by accident. I use mermaid class diagrams since 2022 and only used `*` and `$`, like mentioned in the documentation.

comments.author: knsv
comments.body:
I agree this will be a problem for people using the question mark. However, that has been a "hidden feature" in the docs, we have been consistent since 2019 * and $. My interpretation is a mistake, and I think we can go ahead.

We could allow question marks as well, but let's keep it in sync with the docs as the first option. In the very unlikely event that this results in outrage, we can add it.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
It looks like it was accidentally added in https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/4534, as it looks like `*` and `$` are the only two values that do anything in https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/05c2a11e3d265d99c21a1a190be75048c1c0e985/packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/class/classTypes.ts#L122-L131, so `/[$*]/` is correct!

Since the `?` doesn't seem to do anything currently, I believe this to be a safe change, even for people already using `?`.
